question: For replicated single-cell RNA-seq comparisons within a cell type, how do biological replication and benchmark conditions affect the reported strengths and limitations of pseudobulk and mixed-model differential expression?
scope: Agent-operated engineering pilot with real historical papers; not an independent researcher trial or a current systematic review.

paper.title: A practical solution to pseudoreplication bias in single-cell studies

cells.text: Cells from one individual are correlated subsamples. The study evaluates type 1 error using simulated inter- and intra-individual variance estimated from real data.
cells.conditions: Within-cell-type comparisons across individuals; a simulation-based reference standard. Do not equate cell count with independent sample count.

paper.title: A practical solution to pseudoreplication bias in single-cell studies

cells.text: The authors report a power advantage for mixed-effects models over pseudo-bulk aggregation in their simulation-based study. Their discussion particularly emphasizes heavy imbalance and within-subject variability large relative to between-subject variability. This conditional finding does not directly overturn rankings from the other papers' different benchmarks.
cells.conditions: Within-cell-type comparisons across individuals; simulations of inter- and intra-individual variance. The additional page-6 passage qualifies the initial abstract-level interpretation. Unequal cells per individual and the within-/between-individual variance ratio matter; this entry does not establish a universal winner.

paper.title: Confronting false discoveries in single-cell differential expression

cells.text: Performance depends on accounting for between-replicate variation. The reported main benchmark compares 14 methods across 18 reference datasets, using concordance between matched bulk and single-cell DE results.
cells.conditions: Matched populations and perturbations are the reference; the concordance metric differs from simulated power and type 1 error. Eighteen reference datasets are distinct from the separate 46-dataset compendium.

paper.title: Confronting false discoveries in single-cell differential expression

cells.text: All six leading methods in the main benchmark aggregate cells within biological replicates. A follow-up GLMM analysis also reports accurate results for specific settings and convergence to pseudobulk performance at 500 or more cells, qualifying a blanket claim that mixed models always perform worse.
cells.conditions: Main 14-method/18-dataset benchmark and separate follow-up GLMM experiments. The reported 25-50 and 500-or-more cell settings are benchmark conditions, not universal design thresholds.

paper.title: muscat detects subpopulation-specific state transitions from multi-sample multi-condition single-cell transcriptomics data

cells.text: The framework retains sample labels within cell subpopulations for replicated condition comparisons. Its main simulation targets an average 200 cells per subpopulation-sample, about 3,600 cells overall, and five repeats per scenario.
cells.conditions: Multi-sample differential-state simulation; cells per sample and simulation repetitions are different quantities. Reference data and simulation design differ from the other two papers.

paper.title: muscat detects subpopulation-specific state transitions from multi-sample multi-condition single-cell transcriptomics data

cells.text: Most pseudobulk and cell-level mixed-model methods perform well for DE, DM and DP and are relatively consistent across simulation repeats. The selected passage supports both method families under these conditions.
cells.conditions: DE: mean expression changes; DM: modality changes; DP: mixture-proportion changes. Do not extend this result to DB, discussed separately as difficult when means do not differ, or infer a universal winner.

evidence.quote: Cells from the same individual share common genetic and environmental backgrounds and are not statistically independent; therefore, they are subsamples or pseudoreplicates.
evidence.interpretation: The authors distinguish individual biological replicates from correlated cells within an individual. This is a claim about the experimental unit, not a method ranking. Agent-prepared interpretation; independent scientific review pending.

evidence.quote: We completed a simulation study that reproduced both the inter- and intra-individual variance structures estimated from real data and documented the effect of intra-individual correlation on the type 1 error rates of the most frequently used single-cell analysis tools
evidence.interpretation: The benchmark uses simulated inter- and intra-individual variance estimated from real data and evaluates type 1 error. These simulations are a different reference standard from Squair's matched bulk/single-cell concordance benchmark. Agent-prepared interpretation; independent scientific review pending.

evidence.quote: Here, we document this dependence across a range of cell types and show that pseudo-bulk aggregation methods are conservative and underpowered relative to mixed models.
evidence.interpretation: The abstract reports greater power for mixed models than pseudo-bulk aggregation in this study. This initial note does not yet extract the imbalance and variance conditions from the discussion; it is not a universal ranking. Agent-prepared interpretation; independent scientific review pending.

evidence.quote: we recommend mixed-effects models based on long-standing statistical justi fications for the analysis of subsamples, including increased power. This is parti- cularly so in scenarios with heavy imbalance and where within- subject variability is large compared to between-subject variability.
evidence.interpretation: The authors qualify their mixed-effects recommendation by emphasizing heavy imbalance and within-subject variability large relative to between-subject variability. This discussion passage refines the initial abstract-level reading without claiming a universal method ranking. Agent-prepared interpretation; independent scientific review pending.

evidence.quote: We compared the performance of the fourteen methods across the entire compendium of the eighteen gold standard datasets. This analysis immediately revealed that all six of the top- performing methods shared a common analytical property. These methods aggregated cells within a biological replicate, to form so- called ‘pseudobulks’, before applying a statistical test
evidence.interpretation: In the reported comparison of 14 methods across 18 matched reference datasets, all six top-performing methods aggregated cells within biological replicates. The performance measure is concordance with matched bulk RNA-seq, not identical to simulation power or type 1 error. Agent-prepared interpretation; independent scientific review pending.

evidence.quote: Here, we show that the relative performance of these methods is contingent on their ability to account for variation between biological replicates.
evidence.interpretation: The authors associate DE method performance with accounting for variation between biological replicates. More cells are not automatically more independent biological replicates. Agent-prepared interpretation; independent scientific review pending.

evidence.quote: In datasets of 25-50 cells, GLMMs could produce accurate results under very speci fic parameter combinations. However, in datasets comprising 500 or more cells, their performance converged to that of pseudobulk DE methods.
evidence.interpretation: The follow-up GLMM comparison reports parameter-sensitive accuracy at 25-50 cells and convergence with pseudobulk at 500 or more cells. These are reported benchmark sizes, not a universal cell-count recommendation. Agent-prepared interpretation; independent scientific review pending.

evidence.quote: To ensure that method performances are comparable and do not suffer from low cell numbers, we simulated an average of 200 cells per subpopulation-sample instance, amounting to a total of ~200 × (S1 + S2)× K ≈3, 600 cells per simulation. Each simulation and method was repeated five times per scenario, and performances were averaged across replicates.
evidence.interpretation: The main simulation aims for an average 200 cells per subpopulation-sample and about 3,600 cells overall; each scenario is repeated five times. These simulation repetitions are distinct from the three biological samples per condition described immediately above the quote. Agent-prepared interpretation; independent scientific review pending.
